articles.title: What is Bovine Colostrum?
articles.summary: An overview of bovine colostrum, its composition, and why PeakVital uses only Grade-A first-milking colostrum.
articles.content: Bovine colostrum is the first milk produced by cows in the 24-48 hours after birth. It is extraordinarily rich in immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM), lactoferrin, growth factors (IGF-1, TGF-β), and proline-rich polypeptides. PeakVital sources only Grade-A, first-milking colostrum collected within 6 hours of birth to maximize bioactive concentration. Unlike many competitors, PeakVital does not use heat treatments that denature these fragile proteins.
articles.author: Dr. Priya Nair, PhD (Nutritional Biochemistry)

articles.title: Gut Health & Colostrum: The Mucosal Barrier
articles.summary: How colostrum's bioactives support tight-junction integrity and reinforce the gut mucosal layer.
articles.content: The gut lining renews itself roughly every 3-5 days. When tight junctions weaken—due to stress, alcohol, NSAIDs, or poor diet—permeability increases, commonly called 'leaky gut'. Secretory IgA in colostrum coats the mucosal surface, neutralizing pathogens before they breach the epithelium. Proline-rich polypeptides and growth factors like IGF-1 accelerate enterocyte repair. A 2023 randomized controlled trial (n=120) showed a 38% reduction in intestinal permeability markers (zonulin) after 8 weeks of 1.5 g/day bovine colostrum supplementation.
articles.author: Dr. Priya Nair, PhD (Nutritional Biochemistry)

articles.title: Immune Resilience: IgG, Lactoferrin & PRPs
articles.summary: A deep-dive into the three primary immune-modulating compounds found in PeakVital colostrum.
articles.content: IgG accounts for ~70% of all immunoglobulins in bovine colostrum and provides passive humoral immunity by binding and neutralizing pathogens. Lactoferrin is an iron-binding glycoprotein with broad-spectrum antimicrobial, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory activity; it also acts as a prebiotic, selectively feeding beneficial Lactobacillus strains. Proline-rich polypeptides (PRPs) are bi-directional immune regulators—upregulating immunity when suppressed, downregulating when overactive—making them relevant for both infection defence and autoimmune support.
articles.author: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD

articles.title: Athletic Performance & Recovery
articles.summary: How IGF-1 and growth factors in colostrum reduce exercise-induced gut permeability and support lean muscle recovery.
articles.content: High-intensity exercise transiently increases intestinal permeability by up to 200%, allowing bacterial endotoxins to enter the bloodstream and trigger systemic inflammation—a key driver of exercise fatigue. Colostrum's IGF-1 and TGF-β counteract this by maintaining mucosal integrity during and after training. Multiple meta-analyses show colostrum supplementation improves peak power output (+8-12%), VO₂max, and reduces post-exercise DOMS markers (CRP, IL-6). PeakVital recommends 2.5 g taken 30 minutes before training.
articles.author: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD

articles.title: Skin Health & Collagen Support
articles.summary: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) and IGF-1 in colostrum accelerate skin cell turnover and support structural collagen.
articles.content: Colostrum contains epidermal growth factor (EGF) at concentrations roughly 100× higher than human plasma. EGF binds to keratinocyte receptors to stimulate proliferation, accelerate wound healing, and support the skin barrier. IGF-1 promotes fibroblast activity, driving collagen and elastin synthesis. A 12-week pilot study demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in skin hydration (+22%), elasticity (+14%), and a reduction in fine lines (-11%) in women aged 35–55 taking 1.5 g/day.
articles.author: Dr. Priya Nair, PhD (Nutritional Biochemistry)

articles.title: Sourcing & Quality Standards
articles.summary: PeakVital's end-to-end supply chain: USDA-certified grass-fed herds, cold-chain collection, and NSF-certified cGMP manufacturing.
articles.content: PeakVital partners exclusively with family-owned dairy farms in the Great Lakes region that maintain USDA Organic and Animal Welfare Approved certifications. Colostrum is collected within 6 hours post-calving, immediately chilled to ≤4°C, and transported in food-grade ISO-certified tankers. At our NSF Sport-certified cGMP facility, colostrum undergoes low-temperature spray drying (≤55°C) to preserve bioactivity, then microbial and heavy-metal testing via ISO 17025-accredited labs. Certificates of Analysis are published on our website for every production lot.
articles.author: PeakVital Quality Assurance Team

articles.title: How to Take PeakVital: Dosing & Timing
articles.summary: Optimal protocols for taking PeakVital powder—including fasting windows, mixing tips, and what to avoid.
articles.content: For maximum absorption, take PeakVital on an empty stomach, ideally 20-30 minutes before breakfast or before exercise. Mix one scoop (1.5 g) in 4-6 oz of room-temperature water or low-acid juice—avoid hot liquids as temperatures above 60°C degrade IgG activity. Do not mix with coffee or acidic beverages. For therapeutic gut-repair protocols, some practitioners recommend 3 g/day (morning and evening doses) for the first 4 weeks, then tapering to a maintenance dose of 1.5 g/day.
articles.author: PeakVital Scientific Advisory Board

articles.title: Is PeakVital Safe for Lactose-Intolerant Individuals?
articles.summary: Clarifying the lactose content of PeakVital and what those with dairy sensitivities should know.
articles.content: PeakVital colostrum powder contains <0.5% lactose per serving, significantly lower than whole milk (4.8%) or whey protein (varies). Most individuals with lactose intolerance tolerate colostrum well because the spray-dry process further reduces the lactose fraction. However, those with a diagnosed IgE-mediated cow's milk protein allergy (CMPA) should consult their allergist before use, as colostrum contains casein and whey proteins. PeakVital is not vegan. Each lot is tested for lactose content; results are available in our published CoA.
articles.author: PeakVital Medical Affairs

articles.title: Colostrum vs. Whey Protein: What's the Difference?
articles.summary: Breaking down the key compositional and functional differences between colostrum and standard whey supplements.
articles.content: Whey protein is primarily a macronutrient delivery vehicle (20-25 g protein per serving), processed from the liquid byproduct of cheese-making and containing minimal bioactives. Bovine colostrum, by contrast, is collected pre-milk and is a concentrated matrix of immunoglobulins, growth factors, antimicrobial peptides, and cytokines—with comparatively lower protein density (~50-60% protein by weight at PeakVital's concentration). They serve different purposes: whey supports muscle protein synthesis; colostrum modulates immunity, repairs gut barrier integrity, and reduces inflammation. Many athletes stack both.
articles.author: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD

articles.title: Colostrum & the Microbiome
articles.summary: How lactoferrin and PRPs in colostrum selectively feed beneficial bacteria and help correct dysbiosis.
articles.content: Lactoferrin acts as a selective prebiotic, reducing available free iron in the gut—a nutrient required by many pathogenic bacteria—while supporting the growth of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species that thrive in low-iron environments. PRPs further regulate the innate immune response to commensal bacteria, reducing unnecessary inflammation from beneficial microbes. Pilot microbiome sequencing studies show that 12 weeks of colostrum supplementation significantly increases Shannon diversity index and raises Akkermansia muciniphila relative abundance, a keystone species associated with metabolic health and gut barrier integrity.
articles.author: Dr. Priya Nair, PhD (Nutritional Biochemistry)

support_tickets.subject: Can I stack colostrum with my current probiotics?

messages.body: I take Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and Bifidobacterium longum daily. Is it safe to add colostrum?

Absolutely — colostrum stacks very well with both strains. Lactoferrin in colostrum acts as a prebiotic that selectively feeds Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species, so it can actually enhance the efficacy of your probiotic regimen. We suggest taking colostrum in the morning on an empty stomach and your probiotics later in the day.
